content: 1. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. It also enhances the drug's levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a substrate of CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of dutasteride by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib's AUC, potentially raising the risk of toxicities. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 5. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Limit elagolix to 150 mg daily and restrict CYP3A inhibitor use to six months. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 7. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of eluxadoline by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2C9/10 inhibitors. 8. Ketoconazole and elvitegravir mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered, ketoconazole should not exceed 200 mg/day, and no dose adjustment is needed for elvitegravir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant concentrations, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Ketoconazole increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. Close monitoring for signs of toxicity is required. 11. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Erythromycin base increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, and ketoconazole reciprocally increases erythromycin base levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma estrogen concentrations and toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of eszopiclone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The eszopiclone dose should not exceed 2 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 15. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal formulations) by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals, and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 16. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of fluoxetine by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 17. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of fluticasone (both inhaled and furoate formulations) by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 19. Ketoconazole decreases the plasma levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, decreasing its efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of iloperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
